Pride and Prejudice

Jane Austen

About this book ↗
My review

Seems to be more for the female gaze - it is a little more girly than the things I’m used to reading - it is cool to see a women’s perspective on romance - one of my friends did say this is a book their mom would like so maybe it is a bit of an outdated view of romance but I do think I still took some good insights from the reading. It is only Jane Austen’s perspective on romance and love but it’s interesting to see how different mens’ (or just myself if I don’t generalize) vs womens’ (or Jane Justen’s) views on romance differ. I read this because it was recommended to me and I wanted to learn more about what women find romantic to maybe improve my own love life. I’m not sure if I learned anything that is super useful for the modern world in regards to romance but I was able to put myself in the shoes of some of the women in the book and learn about the pressures to marry and how much your society and community can push this idea on to young women - that they need to marry or something like marriage is their whole life purpose - which is not true at all and kinda undermines how incredibly amazing and capable women are. Things are definitely different now in modern times than when this book was written and the time period it is based in, but I think those fears and concepts or stories about marriage are still relevant - like women still get pushed like fairy tale marriages and these sort of things - which I don’t know if its good or bad I’m just saying my observation. I think I’m a pretty good people person but I do anyways still sometimes have a hard time understanding women.It’s interesting because in a lot of ways there really isn’t anything different between men and women but sometimes it feels like we are completely different species who talk different languages. I did gain some understanding around the fears and pressures for women to marry - which I actually do think are relevant still today - even if it looks maybe a little different. I think it is still generally the common opinion or preference of parents that their daughters get married and a lot of men including myself still make marriage a goal for themselves. Is marriage an outdated concept? I have no idea. Is marriage as a custom good or bad for society? Idk - but I do know that it works for some people and it takes a lot of effort and commitment and it is not easy. I have never done it before - but it’s one of those things that I see more as a very deeply human challenge or spiritual pursuit that two people work on together or something like that rather than a romance or drama. I’m not sure about all the romance or that stuff but I would like to take up that the challenge someday anyways in whatever way marriage can be done well in modern times. I guess part of the challenge is figuring that out together as team. (I might update this review later - I was mostly listening to it as an audio book and missed a lot of the parts in the plot but these are my take aways from what I did catch)

Bhagavad Gita

Traditionally attributed to Vyasa

About this book ↗
My review

I like to read spiritual and religious texts to mog on the dads because I am critical of men (including myself - I am harsh on myself as well). Like “yo did you read your bible today?” - I’m not actually super religious but I would be lying if I said spirituality and religion are not a core part of my life. I do have my own beliefs and personal practices and opinions and I like learning and reading these types of texts. I always get some new insights and I find them calming and grounding when I’m facing a lot of uncertainty or pain in my life. I like the Bhagavad Gita because it is sort of timeless - the bible sometimes the stories in it are hard to put parallels or apply to modern life at least I find some of them to be challenging - there are many stories in the bible that I really love a lot but in general its kinda difficult for me - but the story in the Bhagavad Gita I think can kinda be applied to any individual human’s life no matter the time they are in and has been much easier for me to grasp. The story is about a war between two opposing branches of the royal Kuru dynasty - the Pandavas and the Kauravas. Although going into war where members of each side will die - the members of these opposing clans are cousins and related and part of the same family. Arjuna the main protagonist in the story - is a warrior prince who is facing deep turmoil and dilemma from having to face his relatives in a war where he knows that people on both sides will die. I like this text because it is literally like the daily struggles of being human - each day you wake up with a duty to do your best and reach for the highest potential for yourself and the world around you. In this pursuit there are sometimes struggles with other humans - not necessarily physical struggles but they can be spiritual or emotional or intellectual or moral - but regardless of the outcome and the fact that you will need to struggle with your neighbors and friends and family and coworkers etc - it needs to be done. Without this struggle - humanity and society would degenerate from entropy. So this book - I love because it gives me the strength to move forward from whatever struggles or conflicts or heartbreaks from the past - you have to keep fighting everyday regardless of these human things. We are all human so we will go through human things but every pain and sorrow and joy is all beautiful in its own way and part of the great cosmic battle for good.

A Short Stay in Hell

Steven L. Peck

About this book ↗
My review

I really enjoyed the book. It was a quick read for an afternoon with an interesting premise. I liked the pacing and subplots but wish there was a happier ending. I was left a bit confused on what this hell was trying to teach its guests. My takeaway is that this is something about human nature and searching and hope. This hell had many emergent qualities of life on Earth. I guess humans will always be human no matter their environment. They will love and grieve and play - form groups and spend their time solving problems and searching for something. On Earth, like in Hell, we hope that someone or something whether it be God or something else can witness and validate our struggles and efforts.
